definition: Sediment means solid matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid, or is deposited by water, wind, or ice.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word sediment. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know sediment should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: When Theo poured the last of the homemade grape juice, a gritty layer of sediment slid out of the bottle and into his glass.
A film is a whisper-thin coating; sediment is a genuine accumulated layer you can see and feel.
Sludge is heavier and thicker than sediment — a dense, oozy mass rather than settled particles.

A deposit is matter laid down and left in place over time, by any slow process — minerals in a kettle, ore in rock. Sediment is a particular kind of deposit: solid particles that settle out of a liquid, or are dropped by water, wind, or ice.

Residue is what remains behind after the rest is gone — the crust after liquid boils away, ash after fire. Sediment exists while the liquid is still present: solid particles that sink and settle at the bottom of it. Sediment settles under; residue is left after.

Silt is fine soil particles carried and dropped by moving water — rivers, floods, deltas. Sediment is the wider category: any solid matter that settles out of a liquid or is deposited by water, wind, or ice. All silt is sediment; grit in juice and coffee grounds are sediment too.

Every winter, meltwater sweeps down from the peaks and slows as it enters Lake Solen, and everything the current carried begins to sink.
Grain by grain, the year's load — pollen, ash from summer fires, dust from the far shore — settles through the still water and comes to rest on the bottom.
The lake never dries, so the layers are never disturbed; each year simply lays a new sheet over the last.
To a limnologist, that bottom sediment is a calendar: drive a hollow tube into it, pull up a core, and ten thousand winters come up in order.
